attempted_claim: Prove or disprove the following root-free metric fold-word rigidity statement: let G be a fixed rank-5 marked graph with all vertices of valence at least 3, and let phi, psi in Out(F5) be primitive root-free lone-axis atoroidal fully irreducible elements with equal stretch factor lambda_phi=lambda_psi (hence equal translation length log lambda) and unique invariant periodic fold lines; encode one minimal period as a cyclic word over elementary fold types (proper full fold, partial fold, improper fold) with edge-index permutations plus the ordered per-fold metric expansion-ratio vector and total transition data; if phi and psi admit representatives on the same G with identical cyclic fold-type words up to graph automorphism and cyclic rotation, identical per-fold expansion-ratio vectors up to rotation, and equal stretch factors, then phi is conjugate in Out(F5) to psi; a complete answer is either a proof that this refined metric fold-word determines the conjugacy class among root-free lone-axis atoroidals on G, or an explicit counterexample pair with full Stallings fold sequences, lone-axis certificates, matching cyclic words and expansion vectors with equal stretch factors, root-free certificates, and a rigorous non-conjugacy certificate via Whitehead, lamination, or axis-bundle invariants that cannot be a proper-power pair.
decisive_failure: No proof or counterexample for the root-free metric fold-word rigidity statement was established. Three bounded computational routes were attempted (order-5 circulant scan, 400k-trial swap-symmetric signed-word search, matrix-first feasibility probe) and only matrix-level feasibility was confirmed. Whitehead, PNP, root-free, and fold-sequence certificates remain unverified, so the target is reported as unresolved rather than claimed.
